workstream: W0 — Stop the bleeding: defects shipping in versionCode 6 right now
goal: A player on the live build can no longer be shown a fake "TEST AD", can no longer get stuck on a screen that never advances, is always shown WHICH arrow blocked them (including with OS reduce motion on), is never left staring at a dead ad button, and the ad pacing survives a cold start — while every text and state colour meets the contrast bar PRODUCT.md already claims.
goal_note: ordering below is by (player or revenue harm) / (effort), highest first
non_goals: Consent management (GDPR/CCPA/COPPA/UMP), ATT, SKAdNetwork — real exposure but a separate compliance workstream, not a live defect fix.
FTUE / tutorial, difficulty curve, daily challenge, notifications, analytics — every one is a different workstream.
iOS: the native board view has not compiled since 2026-09-01. The reduce-motion fix lands in shared TS and will apply to iOS when it builds, but nothing here is verified on iOS.
Building the DESIGN.md toast component, a settings screen, level→level transitions, or any new motion. W0 removes defects; it adds no juice.
Replacing the emoji/text control glyphs (back, theme, sound, hint, stars) or the raster wordmark — art workstream.
Any change to the retained native board view, the exit protocol, or the 2-trail / 4-node perf ceilings.

steps.title: Strip the simulated TEST AD out of production builds
steps.what: src/ui/ads.tsx ships a fully functional fake-ad modal into the Play build. `AdHost` (ads.tsx:60-133) renders a panel reading `TEST AD` / `A word from our sponsor` / `Real LevelPlay ads appear in a dev build.` (ads.tsx:94-101), and App.tsx:85 mounts it unconditionally (`{!PERF_MODE && <AdHost palette={p} />}`). `showFakeAd()` (ads.tsx:49-54) is reached from `Ads.showInterstitialIfDue()` (ads.tsx:289) and `Ads.showRewarded()` (ads.tsx:311) whenever `nativeAvailable()` (ads.tsx:146-148) is false — which in a production build is exactly the state left behind when `initAds()` hits its catch (ads.tsx:231-236). CHANGE: gate every simulated-ad entry point on Metro's build-time `__DEV__` constant, not on a runtime check. `AdHost` body begins `if (!__DEV__) return null;`; `showFakeAd` begins `if (!__DEV__) return Promise.resolve(false);`; and in `showInterstitialIfDue` the non-native branch must return WITHOUT resetting the pacing counter (today ads.tsx:288 sets `finishedGames = 0` even though no ad was shown). Runtime checks such as `Constants.executionEnvironment` (ads.tsx:156) cannot work here: they do not remove the strings or the component from the shipped bundle. If the grep in the acceptance criteria still finds the strings, plan B is to move the simulated host into its own module (e.g. src/ui/devAdHost.tsx) and reach it only through a `require()` inside an `if (__DEV__)` block, leaving ads.tsx with no reference to it.
steps.why: Audit finding: 'the simulated TEST AD modal is compiled into and mounted in production builds and is the fallback whenever initAds() fails'. Confirmed by reading App.tsx:85 and ads.tsx:49-54,146-148,231-236,289,311. Harm is threefold: a real player who launches offline or hits a LevelPlay init failure is shown a panel that says the app's own ads are fake; that panel is a plausible Google Play policy problem (deceptive/placeholder ad UI in a shipped app declaring AD_ID in app.json); and every impression served through it earns exactly zero. Expo Go and the web build keep the simulated path, so every ad-gated flow stays testable in development.
acceptance: `npx expo export --platform android` produces a bundle in which `grep -R "TEST AD" dist/` and `grep -R "A word from our sponsor" dist/` both return zero matches.

In a release build (`npx expo run:android --variant release`) with the device in airplane mode from cold start, finishing two levels and pressing Next level shows NO modal of any kind and advances straight to the next level. Confirmed by screen recording.
In the same airplane-mode release build, `Ads.showRewarded()` resolves false without rendering anything (observable as: the lose panel's Continue button does not open any modal).
In Expo Go (`npm start`) the simulated TEST AD modal still appears for both the rewarded and the interstitial flow — development testability is unchanged.
`Ads.showInterstitialIfDue()` does not zero the pacing counter on any path where no ad was actually displayed.
steps.verification: Two parts. (1) `npx expo export --platform android` then `grep -R "TEST AD" dist/` — this exercises the exact failing path because the defect IS the presence of that component in the production bundle; a zero-match grep on the minified output is direct proof Metro eliminated it, and a non-zero match proves the `__DEV__` guard did not strip it and plan B is needed. (2) `npx expo run:android --variant release` on the API 31 emulator with `adb shell svc wifi disable && adb shell svc data disable` BEFORE first launch, so `initAds()` takes its catch branch — the precise state that produces the fake ad today — then play two levels and record with `adb shell screenrecord --time-limit 20 /sdcard/w001.mp4 && adb pull /sdcard/w001.mp4`. Before applying the fix, run step (2) on the current HEAD and confirm the TEST AD panel DOES appear; without that pre-fix capture there is no proof the change touched the broken path.
steps.risk: Ships alone, a production build whose initAds() failed now has NO ad path at all and the lose panel's 'Continue +♥ (ad)' button becomes a dead control that does nothing when tapped. This step MUST ship in the same release as W0-04 (which makes an unavailable rewarded ad visibly unavailable). Rollback: the guards are three one-line `if (!__DEV__)` early returns; reverting them restores current behaviour exactly. No flag needed — `__DEV__` IS the flag, and it is build-time so it cannot be toggled wrong at runtime.
steps.brand_perf_check: FLAG TEST: n/a — no arrow is animated, no Skia node is added or removed; the change is confined to a React modal outside the board tree. Perf ceilings untouched (still 2 exit trails, still at most 4 feedback nodes). Brand gates: removes a busy hyper-casual modal from the shipping app, so it moves toward the PRODUCT.md gates rather than against them.

steps.title: Boot backstop: the app must always reach the menu
steps.what: Three separate paths can leave a player on a screen that never advances, and none has a fallback. (a) src/ui/SplashScreen.tsx:47-49 and :53-56 are the only two `onDone` call sites and both fire from a Reanimated completion callback via `runOnJS`. (b) App.tsx:23 destructures only the first element of `useFonts(...)`; expo-font's hook returns `[loaded, error]` (node_modules/expo-font/build/FontHooks.d.ts:18), so a font-load error leaves `fontsReady` false forever and App.tsx:54 returns a bare background-coloured `<View>` — no splash, no menu, no text. (c) App.tsx:30-34 `initSaveSystem().then(...)` has no `.catch`, so a rejection leaves `ready` false and produces the same blank screen. `grep -rn AppState src/` returns 0 hits. CHANGE: (a) in SplashScreen, add a `firedRef` one-shot guard so `onDone` runs at most once from any source; start `setTimeout(finish, SPLASH_MAX_MS)` on mount with `SPLASH_MAX_MS = 4000` — derived from the file's own timeline, `withDelay(2250, withTiming(..., 380))` at SplashScreen.tsx:47 completes at 2630 ms, leaving 1370 ms of headroom; and subscribe `AppState.addEventListener('change', ...)` so that on return to 'active', if `Date.now() - mountedAt >= SPLASH_MAX_MS`, finish immediately — a JS timer does NOT fire while Android has the app paused, so the timer alone is not a backstop. (b) `const [fontsReady, fontError] = useFonts({...})` and treat `fontsReady || fontError !== null` as ready, so Fredoka silently degrades to the system font instead of a blank screen. (c) `.catch(() => setReady(true))` on the initSaveSystem chain — SaveSystem falls back to its MemoryStore (saveSystem.ts:52), so the game is playable and only that session's progress is lost.
steps.why: Audit finding 'SPLASH HAS NO BACKSTOP', extended by two further no-backstop paths I found reading App.tsx. This is the only class of defect in W0 that costs 100% of the affected player — they cannot reach the game at all, and the only recovery available to them is uninstalling. The AppState half is required by a recorded project scar: a visibility-critical property that only settles from an animation callback needs a deterministic settle that changes the React tree, and JS timers do not run while Android has the app paused.
acceptance: With SplashScreen.tsx temporarily patched so neither `onDone` call site can fire (comment out both `runOnJS(onDone)` lines), a fresh launch still shows the menu within 5 s. Confirmed by screen recording.

With the same patch applied, launching the app and pressing HOME 1 s into the splash, waiting 8 s, then returning to the app shows the menu within 1 s of returning — not a stuck splash. Confirmed by screen recording. This is the AppState path; the JS timer cannot cover it.
`onDone` is observed to run exactly once when the splash completes normally AND the user taps to skip at the same moment (add a temporary counter log; `adb logcat` must show one increment, not two).
With `useFonts` temporarily forced to return `[false, new Error('x')]`, the app reaches the menu and renders readable text in the platform default font — no blank screen.
With `initSaveSystem` temporarily forced to reject, the app reaches the menu, Play starts level 1, and the game is playable.
steps.verification: `npx expo run:android --variant release` on the API 31 emulator with each failure injected in turn (the injections above are three one-line temporary edits, reverted before commit), recording each launch with `adb shell screenrecord --time-limit 15 /sdcard/w002.mp4 && adb pull /sdcard/w002.mp4`. Injecting the failure is what makes this a real verification: the shipped bug is 'when the completion callback never arrives the player is stuck', so the test must be run with the callback removed — launching a healthy build proves nothing, because the healthy build already works. The HOME-press variant is the only way to exercise the AppState branch, since a foreground JS timer would mask it.
steps.risk: A too-short backstop would cut the splash animation off early for slow devices. 4000 ms is 1.5x the scripted 2630 ms end, so this only fires when something has genuinely failed; if a slow cold start is ever observed to trip it, raise the constant rather than removing the backstop. The font fallback changes typography if a font error ever occurs — that is strictly better than a blank screen, and it only happens in a state that is currently fatal. Rollback: all three changes are additive guards; reverting restores current behaviour. No flag — a backstop behind a flag defaults to the broken state.
steps.brand_perf_check: FLAG TEST: n/a — no arrow animates, no Skia node added; SplashScreen is outside the board tree and unmounts before GameScreen exists. Brand gates: unaffected; the splash's visible motion is unchanged in the healthy path.

steps.title: Reduce-motion players must still be told which arrow blocked them
steps.what: All three feedback drivers use Reanimated's default `reduceMotion: ReduceMotion.System`: src/ui/BoardView.tsx:842 (blocker flash), :887 (blocked bump), :934 (hint pulse) and the Skia twins src/ui/StaticBoardSurface.native.tsx:264, :308, :348. With OS reduce motion on, `getReduceMotionFromConfig` (node_modules/react-native-reanimated/src/animation/util.ts:149-155) makes withTiming assign the final value on the first frame, so every reader sees k=1 permanently. Evaluated at k=1 against src/ui/feedbackCurves.ts: `blockerOpacityAt(1) = 1 - 1*1*(3-2*1) = 0`, so the blocking arrow is drawn at opacity 0 and is NEVER visible; the bump colour interpolation (BoardView.tsx:894-902, StaticBoardSurface.native.tsx:315-318) evaluates `eased = 1` and returns pure `ink`, so the tapped arrow does not turn magenta either; and `blockedBumpAt` is already forced to 0 by the existing `reducedMotion` guard. Net: the player taps a blocked arrow, loses a heart, and the board shows nothing at all. (CORRECTION to the audit brief: the hint is NOT lost. Its accent tint is a static prop on both renderers — BoardView.tsx:952-953 `stroke={palette.accent}` and StaticBoardSurface.native.tsx:360 `color={accent}` — only the stroke pulse flattens.) FIX, two parts. (1) Pass `reduceMotion: ReduceMotion.Never` (import `ReduceMotion` from 'react-native-reanimated'; the enum is exported at node_modules/react-native-reanimated/lib/typescript/index.d.ts:12 and the field is on TimingConfig at animation/timing.d.ts:16) in all six withTiming configs, and skip starting the driver entirely when the component's `reducedMotion` prop is true. This removes the split-brain where the JS `useReducedMotion()` value (BoardView.tsx:191) and Reanimated's UI-thread `isReduceMotionOnUI` could disagree, and makes the render code — not Reanimated — decide what degrades. (2) Move the decision into pure worklet functions in src/ui/feedbackCurves.ts, which is a `.ts` file and therefore collected by the existing runner (jest.config.js testMatch `**/src/**/__tests__/**/*.test.ts` never collects `.tsx`): add a `reducedMotion` parameter to `blockerOpacityAt` and `blockerStrokeSwellAt`, and extract the two inline expressions into `blockedFlashMixAt(k, reducedMotion)` (0 = heart, 1 = ink) and `hintStrokeSwellAt(k, reducedMotion)`. Then thread `reducedMotion` into `BlockerArrow` and `HintArrow` in both renderers (today only `ShakingArrow` receives it) and call the shared functions instead of the inline maths at BoardView.tsx:894-902,:938-941 and StaticBoardSurface.native.tsx:267-270,:315-318,:351-354. WHAT THE NON-ANIMATED FALLBACK RENDERS — the blocking arrow is drawn SOLID `palette.heart` at 1.6x the resting stroke at full opacity, held for the whole BLOCKER_FLASH_MS (650 ms), then hard-cut by the unmount timer that already exists in BoardView.tsx (blockerCleanupTimer, BLOCKER_FLASH_MS + 40); the tapped arrow is drawn solid `palette.heart` at the resting stroke with zero translation, held for BLOCKED_BUMP_MS (300 ms), then hard-cut by shakeCleanupTimer; the hint arrow keeps its static accent tint at a constant 1.45x stroke with no oscillation. The player sees exactly two magenta arrows — the one they tapped and the one in the way — with no movement, no fade and no size oscillation. A static recolour is not vestibular motion, so this is the correct reduce-motion degradation rather than a suppression.
steps.why: Audit finding 'REDUCE-MOTION BUG'. The blocker flash is the game's ONLY explanation of its core rule; there is no tutorial (`grep -rn 'tutorial|onboard|first.?run|how to play' src/` = 0 hits), so a reduce-motion player loses hearts with no way to learn why. Level 1 has ~32% clearable arrows, so a naive tap is ~68% likely to be a mistake — this population is being taught nothing while losing at that rate. Secondary: Reanimated's Android reduced-motion source is `Settings.Global.TRANSITION_ANIMATION_SCALE` (node_modules/react-native-reanimated/android/src/main/java/com/swmansion/reanimated/NativeProxy.kt:329) and scripts/perf/android/benchmark.mjs:351 sets `transition_animation_scale 0` on every run, so every perf number this project owns was measured in the broken variant.
acceptance: Unit, encoding the pre-fix failure: `blockerOpacityAt(1, false)` is ~0 (the current shipped behaviour, kept as a regression anchor) while `blockerOpacityAt(k, true) === 1` for every k in [0, 1]; `blockedFlashMixAt(k, true) === 0` for every k in [0, 1]; `hintStrokeSwellAt(k, true) === 1.45` for every k in [0, 1]. Extend src/ui/__tests__/feedbackCurves.test.ts (existing describes at lines 8 and 27).

DEVICE, and this is what actually closes the step: with `adb shell settings put global transition_animation_scale 0` and the app force-stopped and relaunched, tapping a blocked arrow on level 1 produces, in a screen recording at 60 fps: the tapped arrow rendered in `heart` magenta for at least 250 consecutive ms, AND the blocking arrow rendered in `heart` magenta at a visibly thicker stroke than its neighbours for at least 600 consecutive ms, AND zero pixels of translation on either arrow across the whole event.
In the SAME recording, both arrows return to plain ink and no ghost remains after 1 s.

With `transition_animation_scale 1` (reduce motion off) the same tap produces the current animated behaviour, unchanged: the tapped arrow lunges and springs back and the blocker fades out. Confirmed by a second recording, so the fix is proven not to have flattened the default experience.
The hint (rewarded) still renders an accent-tinted arrow in BOTH reduce-motion states.
steps.verification: Pre-fix first: on the current HEAD build, `adb shell settings put global transition_animation_scale 0`, `adb shell am force-stop com.danteb.arrows` (the value is captured once at module init — node_modules/react-native-reanimated/src/ReducedMotion.ts:16 — so a relaunch is mandatory), relaunch, tap a blocked arrow, record with `adb shell screenrecord --time-limit 8 /sdcard/pre.mp4 && adb pull /sdcard/pre.mp4`, and confirm NOTHING changes colour. Then repeat on the fixed build into post.mp4. This exercises the original failing path because `transition_animation_scale 0` is the exact global that drives Reanimated's reduce-motion flag (NativeProxy.kt:329) — the same signal a real accessibility user sets — and the recording, not the unit test, is what shows the arrows. Restore with `adb shell settings put global transition_animation_scale 1` afterwards. `npm test` covers the curve maths only and is explicitly NOT sufficient evidence here: this project has a scar from transform work verified by tsc alone.
steps.risk: Skia and react-native-svg must be checked separately — the same curve change must be seen in BOTH recordings (native Skia overlay and, on web, the SVG layer), because they are different renderers reading the same functions. Second risk: `useReducedMotion()` is read once per mount (BoardView.tsx:191); toggling the OS setting while the app is alive will not re-render the board — acceptable, matches Reanimated's own module-init capture, but must be stated so a tester does not report it as a new bug. Rollback: `ReduceMotion.Never` and the extra parameters are additive and default to today's behaviour when `reducedMotion` is false, so reverting the six config objects restores the current build. No runtime flag: a flag defaulting OFF would leave the accessibility population in the broken state, which is the whole defect.
steps.brand_perf_check: FLAG TEST: PASSES. No arrow that is still in the static layer is animated — `BlockerArrow`, `ShakingArrow` and `HintArrow` are the existing Skia nodes drawn OVER the retained native board, and no new node is added (still at most 4: pressed, blocker, shaking, hint; still 2 concurrent exit trails per exitAnimationConfig.ts:43). No `excludedArrows` mask rebuild is introduced. In the reduced-motion state the change is perf-NEUTRAL-to-positive: not starting the three withTiming drivers means the derived values are constants and the UI thread does strictly less work than today, and it avoids three settle-triggered React re-renders per blocked tap (Reanimated 4.5.1 ships FORCE_REACT_RENDER_FOR_SETTLED_ANIMATIONS on by default — inference from the capability brief, not measured here). Brand gates: no glow, no gradient, no particles; the fallback is a solid recolour in the existing `heart` role, and direction is still carried by arrow shape, never colour.

steps.title: A rewarded ad that cannot be served must say so, not fail silently
steps.what: Both rewarded call sites treat 'no ad' as 'do nothing'. src/ui/GameScreen.tsx:172 `if (!earned) return; // stay on the lose panel; Retry still works` and GameScreen.tsx:188 `if (!earned) return;` — the player taps 'Continue +♥ (ad)' or the 💡 button, the button un-dims, and absolutely nothing happens or is said. `Ads.showRewarded()` (ads.tsx:296-312) returns false both for a genuine no-fill (`isAdReady()` false, ads.tsx:298) and for a show failure. CHANGE, three parts. (1) In src/ui/ads.tsx, track rewarded readiness from the listener callbacks that already exist (`onAdLoaded` ads.tsx:206, `onAdLoadFailed` :207, `onAdClosed` :213, `onAdDisplayFailed` :220) into a module boolean, and expose `Ads.rewardedReady` plus `Ads.subscribeRewardedReady(cb)` — event-driven, no polling and no new timers. In a build where `nativeAvailable()` is false, readiness is false. (2) In GameScreen, drive the hint HeaderButton's `active` prop (GameScreen.tsx:226-231) and the lose panel's Continue button `disabled` prop (GameScreen.tsx:273-290) from that readiness instead of only from `adBusy`, so an unservable ad reads as an unavailable control rather than a dead tap. (3) When a show is nevertheless attempted and returns false, render a single `inkDim` line of copy — on the lose panel, replace the existing `panelSub` text (GameScreen.tsx:268-272, style at :547) with 'No ad available right now — Retry is free'; during play, show a one-line label in the header row beside the '{remaining} left' counter (GameScreen.tsx:218-220) reading 'Hint unavailable' for 2 s. Reuse the existing `styles.diffLabel` / `styles.panelSub` typography; add no new component.
steps.why: Audit finding: 'rewarded no-fill being a silent no-op with no player feedback'. The rewarded ad is the one format positively associated with retention and it is the only in-game teaching aid the player can reach after the FTUE gap; a control that visibly does nothing trains the player to stop trying it, which costs both the impression and the assist. This step is also the safety net that lets W0-01 ship: once the fake ad is stripped from production, an initAds failure makes both these buttons permanently unservable, and without this step they become dead controls.
acceptance: In a release build launched in airplane mode (so no rewarded ad can ever load), the 💡 hint button renders in its unavailable state from first paint and tapping it produces no state change and no busy spinner.
In the same build, the lose panel's 'Continue +♥ (ad)' button renders disabled, and the panel's subtitle line reads 'No ad available right now — Retry is free'. Confirmed by device screenshot.

With network restored and a rewarded ad loaded, both controls render in their available state within 5 s of the ad loading, without the player leaving the screen — proving the readiness subscription pushes rather than requiring a remount.

Every state change above is driven by a listener callback: `grep -n 'setInterval\|setTimeout' src/ui/ads.tsx` shows no new polling timer beyond the two existing 15 s reload retries at ads.tsx:189 and :207.
The unavailable state of both controls meets the contrast gate set in W0-07 — an unavailable control must still be legible, not invisible.
steps.verification: `npx expo run:android --variant release`, launched with `adb shell svc wifi disable && adb shell svc data disable` applied BEFORE first launch so `initAds()` genuinely fails — that is the exact state that produces today's silent no-op, and it is the only way to reach the `!earned` branch on demand. Capture `adb exec-out screencap -p > w004-nofill.png` on the lose panel, then re-enable the radios with `adb shell svc wifi enable`, wait for a load, and capture `w004-ready.png` from the same screen without navigating away. Run the same two captures on the current HEAD first: the pre-fix pair must show an identical, enabled-looking button in both states, which is the defect. `npm test` cannot verify this — GameScreen.tsx is a `.tsx` file and the jest runner collects only `.test.ts` (jest.config.js).
steps.risk: Getting readiness wrong in the pessimistic direction hides a working hint button; keep the fallback 'if in doubt, allow the tap and let showRewarded decide', so a readiness bug degrades to today's behaviour plus a message rather than to a hidden feature. The 2 s in-play label is new text on the board screen — it must sit in the existing header row and must never overlay the board (PRODUCT.md 'the board is sacred'). Rollback: the readiness plumbing is additive; reverting the two prop bindings restores current behaviour. Worth shipping behind a simple module constant (`REWARDED_READINESS_UI = true`) so it can be turned off in a hotfix without a code change.
steps.brand_perf_check: FLAG TEST: PASSES — no arrow is animated, no Skia node added or removed, nothing touches the static layer or the exit trail slots. Brand gates: no new modal, no confetti, no busy hyper-casual affordance; one line of existing-style `inkDim` copy in a row that already exists, and a state change on controls that already exist. 'Flow over menus' is respected — nothing new is inserted between the player and the next tap.

steps.title: initAds must retry, and a load failure must not disable ads for the whole session
steps.what: src/App.tsx:35 calls `initAds()` exactly once, un-awaited and with no `.catch`, and it is never called again for the life of the process. Worse, inside src/ui/ads.tsx the assignments that switch the app onto the real SDK — `lpInterstitial = inter; lpRewarded = rew; levelPlayApi = LevelPlay;` (ads.tsx:228-230) — happen only AFTER `await inter.loadAd()` (ads.tsx:202) and `await rew.loadAd()` (ads.tsx:226). Any rejection from either call jumps to the catch at ads.tsx:231 and nulls all three, so a first-request failure permanently disables the native path even though `LevelPlay.init` succeeded and the listeners' own 15 s reload retries (ads.tsx:189, :207) are wired up and would have recovered. CHANGE: (1) assign `lpInterstitial`, `lpRewarded` and `levelPlayApi` immediately after the init callback resolves (ads.tsx:184) and before any `loadAd()`, and call `inter.loadAd()` / `rew.loadAd()` with `.catch(() => {})` so a failed first request is handled by the existing listener retry rather than by tearing down the SDK handles; (2) make `initAds()` idempotent and retryable — an `initState: 'idle' | 'running' | 'ready' | 'failed'` module variable, with a bounded retry on failure (e.g. 3 attempts at 5 s / 15 s / 45 s, then stop) so a device that boots the app before the network is up still monetises; (3) in App.tsx add the `.catch(() => {})` that the un-awaited promise currently lacks.
steps.why: Audit finding: 'the fallback whenever initAds() fails (it is called once, never retried)'. Reading the file shows the failure is wider than the audit recorded: it is not only that init is never retried, it is that a single rejected `loadAd()` promise discards a successfully initialised SDK. A player who cold-starts on a train, or whose first ad request no-fills, earns zero for the entire session even after connectivity returns.
acceptance: Release build launched in airplane mode; after 60 s with the radios re-enabled, `adb logcat` shows a further LevelPlay init attempt and, on success, `Ads.rewardedReady` (from W0-04) flips to true and the hint button becomes available WITHOUT restarting the app.
Retries are bounded: with the radios left off, `adb logcat` shows at most 3 further init attempts and then no more for 10 minutes — no unbounded retry loop draining battery.
Calling `initAds()` a second time while an attempt is in flight does not start a second LevelPlay init (assert via a temporary log line counting entries to the init block).

With LevelPlay init succeeding but the first `loadAd()` rejecting (simulate by temporarily throwing from the inter.loadAd call), `nativeAvailable()` still returns true and the app stays on the real SDK path — this is the specific regression being fixed.
No behaviour change in Expo Go or on web: `initAds()` still returns early at ads.tsx:155-156.
steps.verification: `npx expo run:android --variant release` on the API 31 emulator. Sequence: `adb shell svc wifi disable && adb shell svc data disable`, cold launch, `adb logcat -s ReactNativeJS:V IronSource:V LevelPlay:V > w005.log` running throughout, wait 30 s, `adb shell svc wifi enable`, wait 90 s, then read w005.log for the retry and the successful init. This exercises the original failing path because the defect is precisely 'the one init attempt happened while the network was down and nothing tried again'; the log timeline is the observable. For the loadAd-rejection half, the temporary throw is required — no network condition reliably makes `loadAd()` reject rather than report through `onAdLoadFailed`, and whether it ever rejects at all is NOT documented in the vendor typings (node_modules/unity-levelplay-mediation/lib/typescript/src/models/LevelPlayInterstitialAd.d.ts says only 'resolves when the ad is loaded'). Note the log lines at ads.tsx:176,180,210,214,232 are `__DEV__`-gated, so a release build needs temporary unconditional logs or a debug build for this check — state which was used.
steps.risk: A retry schedule that is too eager wastes battery and can trip mediation rate limits; bound it at 3 attempts as specified and never retry once `initState === 'ready'`. Moving the handle assignment before `loadAd()` means `nativeAvailable()` can now be true while no ad is actually loaded — harmless, because both public methods already gate on `isAdReady()` (ads.tsx:273, :298), and W0-04's readiness flag reports the true state to the UI. Rollback: revert ads.tsx; the retry lives entirely in that file. Ship the retry behind a module constant `AD_INIT_RETRIES = 3` so it can be set to 0 in a hotfix.
steps.brand_perf_check: FLAG TEST: n/a — no arrow, no Skia node, no board code touched. Perf: the retry adds at most 3 timers over the app's lifetime, none on the UI thread and none during gameplay rendering. Brand gates: unaffected — no player-visible surface changes in this step.

steps.title: Persist the interstitial counter and show one after a loss
steps.what: src/ui/ads.tsx:255 `let finishedGames = 0` is a module-level in-memory variable. It is not in `SaveSystem.persistenceKeys` (src/core/saveSystem.ts:41-50), so it resets on every cold start and a player who kills the app between levels — the exact session shape PRODUCT.md describes — reaches `GAMES_PER_INTERSTITIAL = 2` (ads.tsx:38) almost never. Separately, the interstitial is only reachable from the win panel: `onNextLevel` (GameScreen.tsx:153-165) awaits `Ads.showInterstitialIfDue()`, while the lose panel's Retry calls `loadLevel(levelIndex)` directly (GameScreen.tsx:301) even though a loss already increments the counter (GameScreen.tsx:148). CHANGE: (1) add `FinishedGamesKey = 'arrows_finished_games'` to src/core/saveSystem.ts and to the frozen `PersistenceKeys` array at saveSystem.ts:41-50, with a `finishedGames` getter and a `setFinishedGames` setter over the existing int store; (2) add the same key to the literal array asserted in src/ui/__tests__/storage.test.ts:36-45 — the store hydrates EXACTLY `SaveSystem.persistenceKeys` (src/ui/storage.ts:20), so a key omitted there silently never hydrates, and the frozen-array assertion at storage.test.ts:35 will fail loudly if it is forgotten; (3) rewrite `Ads.registerGameFinished()` and `Ads.showInterstitialIfDue()` (ads.tsx:257-290) to read and write through SaveSystem instead of the module variable, and to zero the counter ONLY after an ad was actually displayed (today ads.tsx:288 zeroes it on the simulated path even when no host is mounted and the promise resolves false immediately); (4) in GameScreen, route the lose panel's Retry through an async handler that awaits `Ads.showInterstitialIfDue()` under the same `setAdBusy` guard `onNextLevel` uses, EXCEPT when the player has just watched the rewarded continue on that same panel — never two ads in one beat.
steps.why: Audit finding 'INTERSTITIAL COUNTER BUG'. Pure revenue: the pacing system exists, is tuned, and effectively does not fire. Adding the loss path roughly doubles the occasions on which a due interstitial can be delivered, at unchanged pacing.
acceptance: PERSISTENCE / MIGRATION: the new key is a plain int in range [0, GAMES_PER_INTERSTITIAL-1] and needs NO widening of the `IntStore` interface (getInt/setInt/deleteKey, saveSystem.ts:12-16) and no change to the boot hydrate contract. It is additive and read with `store.getInt(FinishedGamesKey, 0)`, so an existing player with no such key reads 0 — worst case one delayed interstitial, once. There is no checksum or version gate in this store (contrast the Lucky Shelf scar), so an unknown key cannot invalidate the other 8 keys: WIPE RISK IS NIL, and the storage test asserts the exact key list so a typo cannot ship silently. The key IS added to `resetProgress()` (saveSystem.ts:146-153) so a reset player is not immediately shown an ad.

`npm test` passes with the updated `storage.test.ts` literal, and a new case asserts a hydrated `arrows_finished_games` value survives `initSaveSystem()` — this is the exact mechanism that would silently drop the key.

DEVICE: finish one level, force-stop the app (`adb shell am force-stop com.danteb.arrows`), relaunch, finish a second level, press Next level — an interstitial IS shown. On the current build this sequence shows none; that difference is the fix.
DEVICE: lose a level (spend all 3 hearts) as the 2nd finished game, decline the rewarded continue, press Retry — an interstitial is shown before the level reloads.
DEVICE: lose a level, WATCH the rewarded continue, then lose again and press Retry — only one ad total is shown in that sequence; the rewarded and the interstitial never stack.
The counter is not zeroed on any path where no ad was displayed (verify by finishing 2 games with ads unavailable, then a 3rd with ads available: the interstitial appears on the 3rd).
steps.verification: `npm test` for the persistence half — and specifically because storage.test.ts:32-47 asserts the frozen key list and that hydration reads exactly that list, it exercises the real failure mode (a new key that never hydrates), not merely the getter that was added. For the behaviour half, `npx expo run:android --variant release` on the API 31 emulator running each of the four sequences above under `adb shell screenrecord`, with `adb shell run-as com.danteb.arrows cat /data/data/com.danteb.arrows/**/RKStorage` (or `adb shell am force-stop` + relaunch as above) used to prove the value survived the process death. Run the cold-start sequence on the current HEAD first and record that NO interstitial appears — without that pre-fix capture there is no proof the change touched the broken path.
steps.risk: This is the only W0 step that touches persisted state; see the migration note in the acceptance criteria. Behavioural risk: an interstitial after a loss is a real tension with PRODUCT.md's calm positioning — see escalation 1. Rollback: the ad-pacing read/write should sit behind a module constant `INTERSTITIAL_AFTER_LOSS = true` so the loss path can be disabled in a hotfix without touching persistence; the persisted key itself is harmless if left in place after such a rollback (it just stops being read).
steps.brand_perf_check: FLAG TEST: n/a — no arrow animated, no Skia node added, no board code touched. Perf: one extra int in the existing single `AsyncStorage.multiGet` at boot (storage.ts:20) and one extra `setInt` per finished game, which coalesces into the existing microtask-batched flush (storage.ts:47-68) — no new native round trip during gameplay. Brand gates: 'flow over menus' is strained by an interstitial after a loss; flagged as escalation 1 rather than decided here. No new UI surface, no clutter.

steps.title: Repair the palette roles that fail the contrast bar PRODUCT.md sets
steps.what: PRODUCT.md:62 states 'Text and arrows meet ≥4.5:1 (body) / ≥3:1 (large) against their surface'. I computed the WCAG 2.x relative-luminance contrast for every role/background pair actually used in the app (script written to the session scratchpad; ship it as `scripts/contrast-audit.mjs` so the numbers are reproducible). SEVEN pairs fail: (1) inactive header glyph — `heartLost` on `surface` = 1.21:1 Daylight / 1.44:1 Ink Night, at src/ui/HeaderButton.tsx:35, which is the 'sound is off' state on HomeScreen.tsx:65; (2) spent heart pip — `heartLost` on `bg` = 1.40:1 / 1.63:1, GameScreen.tsx:395, a meaningful non-text graphic that WCAG 1.4.11 wants at 3:1; (3) the in-game 'LEVEL N' label — `accentLight` on `bg` at fontSize 18 bold = 3.49:1 Daylight, GameScreen.tsx:209 with styles.levelLabel at :504-508 (18 px bold is below the WCAG large-text threshold, so the 4.5:1 body gate applies); (4) the perfect-streak line — `accentLight` on `surface` at 13 px = 3.01:1 Daylight, GameScreen.tsx:307-311 / styles.streak :562-566; (5) secondary copy — `inkDim` on `surface` = 4.43:1 Daylight, used by the panel subtitle (GameScreen.tsx:268, 14 px) and the Retry button label (GameScreen.tsx:303, 16 px bold — still below the 18.66 px bold large-text threshold); (6) the Super Hard tier label — `heart` on `bg` = 4.16:1 Daylight at 12 px (GameScreen.tsx:218) and 15 px (HomeScreen.tsx:74); (7) the Hard tier label — `accent` on `bg` = 4.18:1 Ink Night at those same sizes. CHANGE: (a) add `scripts/contrast-audit.mjs` computing every used pair, and `src/ui/__tests__/theme.test.ts` (a `.ts` file, so the existing runner collects it — jest.config.js testMatch never collects `.tsx`) asserting each pair meets its gate, so the suite fails if a token regresses; (b) fix the two worst by SHAPE as well as colour, which is also the more brand-correct answer: split HeaderButton's overloaded `active` prop (HeaderButton.tsx:8, :35) into `disabled` (availability — may stay dim, WCAG exempts disabled controls) and a state that is conveyed by the glyph itself, so sound-off shows a struck/muted glyph rather than only a faint one, and give the inactive-state glyph its own token at ≥3:1 as a UI component; render spent heart pips as an OUTLINE (stroke in `inkDim`) rather than a paler fill (GameScreen.tsx:392-398), which reaches 3:1 without adding a colour; (c) adjust the remaining tokens by the smallest change that clears the gate, solved for by the audit script rather than picked by eye, and update the contrast line in DESIGN.md:44 to the measured values.
steps.why: Audit finding 'six palette roles fail their own contrast targets'. My own measurement (the script named above) finds seven role/context pairs failing, and confirms the worst at 1.21:1. This is a promise the product documentation makes to players and does not keep; the sound-off state in particular is the ONLY indication that sound is off and it is effectively invisible in Daylight.
acceptance: `node scripts/contrast-audit.mjs` prints every role/background/size-class triple used in the app with its computed ratio and its gate, and exits 0 with zero failures in BOTH Daylight and Ink Night. Before the fix the same script must exit non-zero listing the seven pairs above — that is the pre-fix failure, captured.
`npm test` includes src/ui/__tests__/theme.test.ts asserting the same gates, so a future token edit that regresses contrast fails CI rather than shipping.
The sound-off state is distinguishable from sound-on in a GREYSCALE conversion of a device screenshot of HomeScreen — i.e. it does not depend on colour alone.
A spent heart pip is distinguishable from a filled one in a greyscale conversion of a device screenshot of GameScreen with 1 of 3 hearts spent.

Side-by-side device screenshots of HomeScreen, GameScreen mid-level, the win panel and the lose panel, in both themes, before and after: the identity is unchanged — still one violet accent, still magenta reserved for hearts and the blocked flash, no new hue introduced, no gradient, no glow. Owner sign-off on these eight screenshots is required before this step is called done.
steps.verification: `node scripts/contrast-audit.mjs` on HEAD (must fail, listing the seven pairs) and after (must pass) — this exercises the defect directly because the defect IS the numeric ratio between two token values, and the script computes it from src/ui/theme.ts rather than from a design doc. Then `adb exec-out screencap -p > w007-<screen>-<theme>.png` for the eight screens above, plus a greyscale conversion of the two state screenshots. The screenshots are mandatory and the maths alone does not close this step: contrast can be fixed in a way that wrecks the look, and this project's rule is that visual work needs owner eyeball acceptance.
steps.risk: Token changes are global — `accentLight`, `inkDim` and `heart` each appear on several screens, so a fix aimed at one label shifts others. Mitigate by preferring per-usage fixes (size or role change at the call site) over token edits wherever the audit script shows the token passes elsewhere; escalation 2 covers the one case where the two readings genuinely diverge. Rollback: theme.ts is a pure data module — reverting it restores the exact current palette, and the audit script and test can stay in place as a failing red marker. No runtime flag; a themed palette behind a flag would double every screenshot.
steps.brand_perf_check: FLAG TEST: n/a — no arrow animated, no Skia node added, no board rendering path touched. Note the arrow `ink` role is NOT in the failing set (17.66:1 / 16.14:1 on bg), so the board itself is untouched — 'the board is sacred' holds. Brand gates: the fix deliberately reaches for shape (struck glyph, outlined pip) before colour, matching PRODUCT.md's 'direction by shape never colour' principle and avoiding the 'decorative color soup' gate; no glow, no gradient, no new accent.

steps.title: Reconcile the missing extra.eas.projectId with appVersionSource: remote
steps.what: eas.json sets `cli.appVersionSource: "remote"` and the production profile sets `autoIncrement: true`, but app.json has no `expo.extra.eas.projectId` — the file has no `extra` block at all. With a remote version source the local `android.versionCode: 6` in app.json is not what EAS uses; the version comes from EAS's own store for the linked project, and with no projectId there is no deterministic link from this working copy to that store. CHANGE: run `npx eas-cli init` (or `npx eas-cli project:info` if the project is already registered under the owner's account) and write the returned id into `app.json` as `expo.extra.eas.projectId`. Then reconcile the version: read the remote value and confirm it is consistent with the last shipped build (git log: `bb63913 release: versionCode 6`). Do not invent or guess the id — it must come from the EAS API against the owner's account.
steps.why: Audit finding: 'app.json has no extra.eas.projectId though eas.json sets appVersionSource: remote'. This is a release-safety defect rather than a player-facing one: a production build whose remote versionCode has drifted below 6 will be built and then rejected by Play as an already-used version code, or — worse — a build could be submitted with a version the team did not expect. It is cheap to close and it blocks a bad surprise on the next release.
acceptance: `npx eas-cli project:info` resolves a project without prompting for a link, i.e. it reads the id from app.json rather than asking.

`npx eas-cli build:version:get --platform android --profile production` returns a versionCode, and that number is >= 6 (the last shipped build, git commit bb63913). If it is < 6 or absent, STOP and escalate — see escalation 5 — because `autoIncrement: true` would then generate a code Play has already consumed.

A production build started with `npx eas-cli build --platform android --profile production --non-interactive` gets past configuration resolution without any interactive prompt — non-interactive is what proves the link is written down rather than supplied by a human at the terminal.
RELEASE.md records the projectId, the remote versionCode source of truth, and the fact that app.json's `android.versionCode` is inert under `appVersionSource: remote`.
steps.verification: The three CLI commands above, run in a clean checkout (`git stash` any local changes first) so the result cannot be produced by uncommitted state or by a cached interactive link in the developer's home directory. `--non-interactive` is the load-bearing flag: it is the only way to distinguish 'configured' from 'a human answered a prompt', which is precisely the failure this step fixes. Do NOT run an actual submit as verification.
steps.risk: Running `eas init` against the wrong account or org creates a second project and would fork the remote version counter — run `project:info` FIRST and only fall back to `init` if it reports no project. If the remote versionCode has already drifted, changing it is an outward-facing release decision, not an engineering one: escalate rather than set it. Rollback: removing the `extra` block from app.json restores the current (broken but known) state; nothing is destroyed locally. No flag applies.
steps.brand_perf_check: FLAG TEST: n/a — configuration only, no runtime code, no arrow, no Skia node. Brand gates: not applicable; nothing player-visible changes.

escalations.question: Should a paced interstitial be shown after a LOSS (on the lose panel's Retry), not only after a win?
escalations.options: (a) Yes, on Retry, at the unchanged every-2-finished-games pacing (W0-06 as written). (b) Win path only, but fix the persistence so the counter survives a cold start — i.e. take half of W0-06. (c) No interstitials at all until a daily-content/retention workstream lands.
escalations.recommendation: (a), with the guard already written into W0-06: never in the same beat as the rewarded 'Continue +♥'. The counter already increments on a loss (GameScreen.tsx:148) — the current build takes the cost of the pacing without ever collecting on it. But this is a taste call about a calm, ad-light game interrupting a player at their most frustrated moment, and PRODUCT.md's 'flow over menus' is a real counterweight, so it is yours, not mine.
escalations.why_it_cannot_be_decided_here: It is a brand/monetisation trade with no measurement available: there is no analytics in the app at all, so neither the revenue gain nor the churn cost can be measured before or after the change.

escalations.question: The in-game 'LEVEL N' label uses `accentLight` at 18 px bold on bg = 3.49:1 (Daylight, measured), below the 4.5:1 body gate. DESIGN.md:44 explicitly licenses accent-light as 'large decorative only ≈3.2:1'. Fix the token or fix the usage?
escalations.options: (a) Change the usage: raise GameScreen's levelLabel from 18 px to 24 px, matching HomeScreen's 24 px where the same token passes the 3:1 large gate. (b) Darken the `accentLight` token until it clears 4.5:1 at 18 px, which changes the look of the Home 'Level N' label too. (c) Keep 18 px and recolour that one label to `accent` (5.42:1 Daylight, measured).
escalations.recommendation: (a). It honours DESIGN.md's own 'large decorative only' license instead of overriding it, keeps one visual identity for the level label across both screens, and it is the only option that changes zero tokens. The cost is a slightly taller game header — a layout change you should see before it ships.
escalations.why_it_cannot_be_decided_here: Two documented requirements diverge: PRODUCT.md:62 sets a blanket 4.5:1 body gate, DESIGN.md:44 carves this token out as decorative. Which document wins is an owner call, and the answer changes the look of two screens.

escalations.question: When no rewarded ad can be served, should the hint be granted for free?
escalations.options: (a) Grant the hint free after a confirmed no-fill (with the same once-per-tap behaviour). (b) Leave the hint button visibly unavailable until an ad loads (W0-04 as written). (c) Always free — drop the ad gate on hints entirely.
escalations.recommendation: (a). The hint is the only in-game teaching aid a new player can reach, and the audit shows there is no tutorial at all; a permanently dim button in a build whose initAds failed removes the feature outright and teaches nothing. Granting it free costs an impression that, by definition, did not exist.
escalations.why_it_cannot_be_decided_here: It trades a monetisation surface against a new-player-comprehension surface, and neither is measurable in-product today (no analytics). It also sets a precedent for how other rewarded placements degrade.

escalations.question: Should the reduce-motion fix also add an in-app 'Reduce motion' toggle, or honour the OS setting only?
escalations.options: (a) OS setting only (W0-03 as written). (b) Add an app-level override, which requires a settings screen that does not exist and a 9th persisted key.
escalations.recommendation: (a). There is no settings screen, PersistenceKeys is deliberately minimal, and the OS setting is the accessible, discoverable control users already know. An in-app toggle is a feature, not a defect fix, and does not belong in W0.
escalations.why_it_cannot_be_decided_here: It is a scope decision about whether W0 is allowed to add a new player-facing surface; I have kept W0 strictly to removing defects.

escalations.question: If `eas build:version:get` returns a remote Android versionCode BELOW 6 (the last code shipped to Play, git commit bb63913), what should be done?
escalations.options: (a) Set the remote version to 6 with `eas build:version:set` before the next production build. (b) Switch eas.json to `appVersionSource: "local"` and let app.json's `android.versionCode` be the source of truth again. (c) Leave it and hand-check the versionCode on every release.
escalations.recommendation: (a), then record in RELEASE.md that app.json's `android.versionCode: 6` is inert while `appVersionSource` is remote. It is one command, it keeps the autoIncrement behaviour the production profile already assumes, and it removes the hand-check from every future release.
escalations.why_it_cannot_be_decided_here: It writes to the owner's EAS account and it directly determines what the next Play submission is numbered — an outward-facing, hard-to-reverse release action. I will not run it.

open_verification_gaps: I did not run, build, launch, or attach a device to this app in this session. Every runtime claim above is EXECUTED-AND-OBSERVED only where I say so; the rest is INFERRED FROM READING the source. Specifically inferred, not observed: the reduce-motion blackout, the fake-ad-in-production fallback, the interstitial counter behaviour across cold starts, and every stuck-screen path. Each step's verification section names the command that would actually observe it.

EXECUTED: the contrast numbers. I wrote and ran a WCAG 2.x relative-luminance script over the exact hex values in src/ui/theme.ts (scratchpad, to be shipped as scripts/contrast-audit.mjs) — those ratios are measured, not quoted. INFERRED: the mapping from role to WCAG size class, which I read out of the StyleSheets. RN honours the OS font-scale setting, so a 16 px bold label that fails the body gate today could cross into the large-text class at 1.3x scale (or a 24 px one could stay body-class if the user shrinks text). Font scaling was NOT measured and the audit script as specified does not model it.

EXECUTED-BY-READING-SOURCE: Reanimated 4.5.1's reduce-motion mechanism — I read node_modules/react-native-reanimated/src/animation/util.ts:149-155, src/ReducedMotion.ts:7-16 and android/.../NativeProxy.kt:329, which is why I can state that `transition_animation_scale 0` is the Android trigger and that the value is captured once at module init. I have NOT confirmed on a device that the harness's setting actually produces the blackout — that is the pre-fix capture W0-03 demands.

Whether Metro/terser actually eliminates the TEST AD string literals under an `if (!__DEV__)` early return is an ASSUMPTION about the bundler, not a fact I verified. W0-01's acceptance is written as a grep over the real export precisely so this cannot be waved through, and it names the plan B if the grep fails.

Whether LevelPlay's `loadAd()` ever REJECTS on no-fill (versus reporting only through `onAdLoadFailed`) is undocumented in the vendor typings I read. W0-05's premise — that a rejected loadAd tears down a successfully initialised SDK — is certain as code (ads.tsx:202/226 precede the assignments at :228-230), but how often it fires in the field is unknown and unmeasurable today.

The revenue impact of W0-06 cannot be measured before or after: there is no analytics, no crash reporting and no remote config in this app, so 'interstitials almost never fire' is a code-reading conclusion with no field data behind it, and the fix will have no field data after it either.

iOS is entirely unverified. The reduce-motion fix (W0-03) lands in shared TypeScript and StaticBoardSurface.native.tsx, so it should apply to iOS, but the native board view has not compiled since 2026-09-01 and nothing in W0 is checked there. Every device acceptance above is Android-only, on the single API 31 emulator this project has.

I corrected one audit claim from the brief: the ad-paid hint does NOT render nothing under reduce motion. Its accent tint is a static prop on both renderers (BoardView.tsx:952-953, StaticBoardSurface.native.tsx:360) and only the stroke pulse flattens. That correction is INFERRED FROM READING and should be confirmed in the same W0-03 recording pass rather than taken on my word.

No perf measurement was run for any step. W0-03's claim that the reduced-motion path becomes cheaper (three drivers not started, three settle-triggered React re-renders avoided) is reasoning from the code plus the capability brief's note about FORCE_REACT_RENDER_FOR_SETTLED_ANIMATIONS — it is NOT measured, and given this project's measurement ceiling (one loaded-host emulator, ~15 ms resolution on the exit phase) a difference that small is probably below the instrument's resolution anyway. Do not quote it as a perf win.
